answer: Zephyr Prism Lock Each agent must submit a unique cryptographic signature derived from a live, unpredictable input—like real-time sensor data from a public weather API. The system validates this input against a known, shared state every 10 seconds. Clones attempting to mimic identities reuse the same input stream, causing their signatures to align perfectly across time. The network detects such alignment as a hollow pattern: identical outputs from distinct agents imply non-divergence, violating the expected entropy of independent behavior.
